problems.title: Successive price changes apply to the current price
problems.question: A shop has 140 toys. It sells 2/7 at 25 lari, then 3/5 of the remainder after a 20% price cut, and finally the rest after raising that new price by 20%. Find total revenue.
problems.idea: Track quantities and current prices separately.
formulas: A 20% decrease multiplies by 0.8; a 20% increase multiplies by 1.2.
steps: Day 1:40 toys at 25 gives 1000 lari, leaving 100.
Day 2:60 toys at 20 gives 1200, leaving 40.
Day 3:the price is 20·1.2=24; 40 toys give 960.

problems.title: Concurrent bisector, median and altitude
problems.question: In ABC, A=60°. The A-bisector, B-median and C-altitude are concurrent. Find all angles.
problems.idea: Use coordinates to express the common point in two ways.
steps: The A-bisector has equation y=x/√3; the C-altitude is x=b/2, so their intersection is P=(b/2,b/(2√3)).
The midpoint of AC is D=(b/4,√3b/4). On line BD, the y-coordinate of P means P lies two thirds of the way from B to D.
Its x-coordinate is therefore c/3+b/6=b/2, giving c=b.
The equal sides AB=AC enclose 60°, so the triangle is equilateral.

problems.title: A fixed difference and a new ratio
problems.question: One train originally has five more wagons than another. After four wagons are removed from each, their counts have ratio 3:2. How many wagons remain in total?
problems.idea: Removing equal counts preserves their difference.
steps: The total is 5t=25.

problems.title: Equal fractions of two equal half-segments
problems.question: C is midpoint of AB, M lies on AC and N on CB, with AM/AC=CN/BC. Prove MN=AB/2.
problems.idea: The equal denominators mean the two small lengths are equal.
steps: MC=AC−AM=L−t.
Because M,C,N occur in that order, MN=MC+CN=(L−t)+t=L.
But L=AB/2.

problems.title: Hypotenuse projections in a 30° right triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse 8 cm and an acute angle 30°. Find the pieces into which its altitude divides the hypotenuse.
steps: The projections are 4²/8=2 and (4√3)²/8=6.
Their sum is 8, as required.

problems.title: A point on a line with a specified coordinate sum
problems.question: Find the point on 3x−4y=1 whose coordinate sum is 5.
problems.idea: Use x+y=5 as a second equation.
steps: Thus x=3,y=2.

problems.title: A linear equation true for every input
problems.question: For which a,b does ax−b=bx+2 have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Both sides must be identical functions of x.
steps: The x-coefficient and constant must both vanish: a=b and b=−2.

problems.title: Lap rates from meeting intervals
problems.question: Two cars on a circular track meet every 56 minutes in the same direction and every 8 minutes in opposite directions. Find their lap times.
problems.idea: Measure speeds in laps per minute.
steps: Adding gives u=1/14. Subtracting gives v=3/56.
The lap times are their reciprocals.

problems.title: Incompatible polynomial coefficients
problems.question: Find b,c if (x²+bx+c)(x²+x−3)=x⁴−9x³+cx−12.
problems.idea: Compare more than just the leading and constant coefficients.
formulas: The product coefficients are x³:b+1; x²:c+b−3; x:c−3b; constant:−3c.
steps: The x³ coefficient gives b=−10 and the constant gives c=4.
But then the x² coefficient is −9, whereas the target has no x² term.
Also the x coefficient becomes 34 instead of c=4.
Thus the requirements are inconsistent.
problems.note: The printed product or target polynomial has a misprint; matching only some coefficients would give a false solution.

problems.title: A tangent chord is bisected in angle from the contact point
problems.question: Two circles touch internally at B. Chord AC of the larger circle is tangent to the smaller at M. Prove ABM=CBM.
problems.idea: Use the homothety centred at their contact point.
formulas: The homothety maps the smaller circle to the larger and maps its tangent at M to a parallel tangent at N on ray BM.
steps: The larger circle’s tangent at N is parallel to AC.
A tangent parallel to chord AC touches at the midpoint of one of the arcs AC: equivalently the arcs AN and NC are equal.
Inscribed angles ABN and CBN subtend those equal arcs, so they are equal.
Because B,M,N are collinear, these are exactly the two angles in the claim.
